doc.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: American music heard around the world
summary: In Germany he heard R&B, Horace Silver, Miles Davis and Coltrane in shops and the airport, and notes Americans take this export for granted.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You know I wanted to ask you to bring that thought home too is you know I find so much beauty in sounds that are produced in the African American community, though they are not in any music method book. You know I’ve never picked up a music method book and have someone tell you how to sing like Aretha Franklin.

Oh, well you won’t find that. No you won’t find that. Well the one thing I can tell you is everywhere I go, I hear American music. Every country in the world, there’ll be some form of American music. I was in Germany last week and I was just amazed, and they were playing some of the R&B and contemporary music, and you know, Barry White and all that, and man I was glad to hear that stuff. I was in a department store and they were just playing, The Manhattans, and Anita Baker, and all these people, then I went in another store and they were playing Horace Silver. In the airport they had all jazz, Horace Silver, Miles Davis, John Coltrane.

Yeah, just piped in. Then in the hotel they had you know, contemporary country & western music, crossing with contemporary R&B music, and I said, man, it’s just amazing. And then it’s amazing too to go back home and see how much people don’t appreciate it.
Yeah. And we just take it for granted.
